name: FHIR Clinical CDR
summary: An open, portable FHIR resource-store accelerator for MongoDB with standard APIs, transparent storage, and explainable search.
description: Imports FHIR JSON, Bundle, and NDJSON data into a reviewed strategy-owned database, preserves canonical resources, materializes mandatory operational search projections, and exposes FHIR read/write/search workflows with visible FHIR Search to MQL compilation.

strategy.description: FHIR database, generation, and search configuration

ui.status_message: Implemented: a minimal, explicitly bounded R4 Patient/Observation interoperability tier; package-backed R5/R6 resource catalogs; JSON/Bundle/NDJSON import; tenant-scoped checkpointed migration runs and reference reports; mandatory search projections and index governance; schema-guarded flat generation plus deterministic patient-centred cohort planning, preview, execution, and quality evidence for R5/R6; CapabilityStatement and downloadable runtime support evidence; create/update/read/type-search; Search-to-MQL explain; optional IG/profile selection with fail-closed external validator enforcement; semantic text/chunk preview; explicit embedding materialization; and Atlas vector retrieval. R4 base-schema validation and synthetic generation, a bundled FHIR profile validator, FHIR resource version history, transactions, conditional operations, subscriptions, terminology services, semantic rebuild jobs, and SMART authorization are not implemented.
ui.story:
Teams moving a FHIR workload to MongoDB usually agree that resources fit the document model, but they still need proof that the result behaves like a usable FHIR system: familiar APIs, predictable identity, declared validation, searchable resources, and a migration path they can inspect. A database layout alone does not provide that confidence.

This accelerator supplies the reusable kernel for that middle ground. Canonical FHIR resources remain recognizable, each configured resource type is isolated in its own collection, and operational search projections sit beside the resource for efficient MongoDB execution. Healthcare Data Lab then exposes the complete journey: inspect the release tier and metamodel, optionally select IGs, profiles, and semantic projections, import or generate data, compile FHIR Search to MQL, execute it against the tenant database, and inspect the result.

The goal is portability and extension rather than claiming to be a finished commercial FHIR server. Customers and partners can use the kernel as a foundation for real migrations, add the conformance, security, history, terminology, and operational controls their product requires, and keep the storage and query behavior visible.
ui.how_it_works:
The activated strategy selects an honest release tier: a deliberately minimal R4 Patient/Observation baseline, or a package-backed R5/R6 FHIR Core baseline. Customers need no IG or profile to begin. Optional local FHIR NPM packages are compiled during activation into checksum-addressed locks, catalogs, search plans, and evidence; optional active profile URLs are selected from those packages. Profile enforcement is a separate opt-in and runs through a configured external validation adapter.

The import boundary accepts a resource, Bundle, or NDJSON batch; requires an active search projection contract for writes; removes client-supplied operational fields; validates at the selected supported level; optionally enforces active profiles; and computes mandatory `_search` and `_compartments` projections through fhir-mql. Synthetic generation is always explicit after activation. Flat recipes serve load/schema tests; versioned cohort blueprints provide deterministic patient graphs, longitudinal rules, previews, and measured quality evidence. Every generated resource passes a fail-closed release-schema guard before the normal persistence boundary. Recipes remain examples, not a write allowlist, and R4 does not claim synthetic generation.

Canonical JSON stays at the document root. `_search` and `_compartments` remain directly indexable siblings, while `_kehrnel` owns control metadata and `_custom` / `_enrichments` reserve customer and partner data that survives canonical FHIR updates. Optional semantic pipeline declarations select simple FHIR paths, profiles, chunking, model metadata, and sidecar storage. Activation validates those declarations but never sends clinical text to an embedding provider; preview remains local, while explicit materialization and search operations call configured embedding and Atlas adapters and store rebuildable sidecars.

At query time, the compiler resolves the search parameters supported for the selected release and resource type and returns the MongoDB collection, filter, sort, limit, and offset. Unknown or unsupported parameters fail closed. Capability, package, index, profile, cohort, and semantic manifests report independent facts instead of one inflated support claim.
benefits: Canonical FHIR JSON remains readable and round-trippable; a narrow, documented operational projection is removed from FHIR-facing responses.
The per-resource-type collection family matches FHIR identity and allows search projections and indexes to evolve independently by resource type.
FHIR Search compilation is visible before execution, so teams can inspect the generated MQL and test whether configured indexes serve their real query shapes.
The activated R4, R5, or R6 support tier and runtime resource catalogs make the implemented scope explicit.
The same kernel supports guided learning, migration rehearsal, synthetic data, and tenant-backed operational experimentation without locking the workload to a managed cloud API.
ui.ideal_for: This strategy is a good fit for teams migrating an existing FHIR integration or data service to MongoDB, building a portable FHIR data foundation, evaluating MongoDB against real FHIR search patterns, or creating a partner product that needs an extensible resource-store kernel. It is especially useful when the team wants to own its infrastructure and application behavior while retaining familiar FHIR APIs and an inspectable MongoDB implementation.
ui.consider_alternatives: Choose a complete FHIR server or managed FHIR service when the project requires broad specification conformance, version history, transactions, conditional interactions, subscriptions, terminology services, implementation-guide and profile validation, SMART authorization, or a supported production platform out of the box. This accelerator is appropriate when teams want a portable MongoDB foundation and intend to own or partner on the remaining product and operational layers. Its conformance claim is limited to the interactions and resource types reported by the active CapabilityStatement.

index_contract.identityIndex: A unique ascending index on `id` is enforced by the storage adapter in each materialized resource collection.
index_contract.searchIndexSource: The active fhir-mql resource configuration supplies resource-specific index definitions to `fhir_ensure_indexes`.
index_contract.summary: A deterministic index manifest is generated from the active mappings, includes the logical-id index, enforces a per-collection budget, and reports unexpected indexes without deleting customer-owned indexes. Indexes are materialized lazily before writes by default.

cards.title: Querying
cards.body: FHIR Search parameters supported for the selected resource type are compiled to MongoDB MQL by fhir-mql. The lab shows the collection, filter, controls, ignored parameters, and execution summary.

cards.title: Migration import
cards.body: FHIR JSON, Bundle entries, and NDJSON are checked against the activated release tier and reviewed resource configuration, projected into operational fields, and persisted through the tenant-bound storage adapter. Large migrations should use bounded NDJSON chunks.

cards.title: Synthetic Generation
cards.body: Use flat recipes for load/schema tests or versioned patient-centred blueprints for cardiometabolic, oncology, and payer journeys. Review a deterministic plan, preview connected patients, and inspect quality evidence before persisting through the normal validation, projection, versioning, and index contract.

cards.title: Schema & Indexes
cards.body: The logical-id index and resource-specific fhir-mql search indexes are mandatory before writes. A generated manifest exposes budgets, drift candidates, and projection versions for targeted maintenance.

cards.title: Core + IG overlays
cards.body: FHIR Core works without a customer IG. Optional checksum-pinned packages add profile and search evidence; discovered profiles remain distinct from profiles actually enforced by a validator.
